skill.name: 1password-credential-lookup
skill.description: Look up website login credentials from 1Password by matching a domain URL and optional username.
skill.summary: Find matching 1Password login items by website domain for assisted sign-in workflows.
skill.author: ClementWalter

security_audit.summary: The executable Python script legitimately uses the 1Password CLI, but it retrieves and prints raw credentials, so the sensitive-access findings are confirmed. Most SKILL.md external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline tool names, not executable shell syntax.

remediation.issue: Raw passwords are returned in command output.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid printing passwords directly; pass secrets only to an approved secure input channel or require explicit user confirmation before disclosure.

remediation.issue: The script enumerates all 1Password items before filtering by URL.
remediation.suggestion: Use the narrowest available 1Password CLI query or document why full item listing is required and keep returned fields minimal.

remediation.issue: The skill encourages automated login with retrieved credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to confirm user authorization and avoid storing, echoing, or logging credentials in transcripts.

semantic_findings.title: Raw Password Exposure in Tool Output
semantic_findings.description: The script returns credential objects that include password values, and the skill documentation advertises password output. This can expose secrets to logs, transcripts, or downstream tools if the agent displays or stores results.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code prints JSON containing extracted credentials, and the documentation states that a single match returns a password field. This is direct evidence of raw secret disclosure.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Vault Enumeration Before Filtering
semantic_findings.description: The script lists all 1Password items before matching by URL. Even though it only returns matches, broad enumeration increases exposure if the process output, errors, or local environment are compromised.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The implementation calls op item list and iterates through all returned item URL metadata. The behavior is clear, but the final returned data is limited to matching candidates.

content.value_statement: Website login automation often fails when agents guess password item names. This skill searches 1Password by website domain and optional username to find the matching login item.
actual_capabilities: Searches 1Password login items by website domain.
Accepts an optional username filter when multiple accounts exist.
Handles x.com and twitter.com as equivalent domains.
Returns item names and usernames when multiple matches are found.
Reports common setup errors for the 1Password CLI.
limitations: Requires the local 1Password CLI to be installed and signed in.
Can expose raw passwords in tool output or transcripts.
Only searches URL metadata available from 1Password items.
Does not verify whether the agent is authorized to use a credential.

use_cases.title: Agent-assisted website sign-in
use_cases.description: Retrieve the correct login item for a known website domain before filling a sign-in form.

use_cases.title: Account selection for shared domains
use_cases.description: List matching accounts for a domain so the user can choose the correct username.

use_cases.title: Password manager workflow testing
use_cases.description: Check whether 1Password items contain usable URL metadata for automated credential lookup.

best_practices: Use the website domain, not a guessed 1Password item name.
Add a username filter when more than one account may exist.
Avoid printing, saving, or sharing passwords returned by the tool.
anti_patterns: Do not guess item names such as GitHub or my github.
Do not use retrieved credentials without user authorization.
Do not paste raw passwords into chat, logs, tickets, or documentation.

faq.question: Does this skill require 1Password?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the 1Password CLI on the local machine and an active sign-in session.

faq.question: Should I search by item name?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed to search by website domain because item names may not match URLs.

faq.question: What happens when multiple accounts match?
faq.answer: The skill can list matching usernames and ask you to choose one before retrieving the credential.

faq.question: Can this expose passwords?
faq.answer: Yes. The underlying script can return password values, so users should avoid logging or displaying them.

faq.question: Does it work with x.com and twitter.com?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill treats those domains as aliases during lookup.

faq.question: Is this safe for unattended automation?
faq.answer: No. Credential retrieval should require user authorization and careful handling of secret output.
